questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) (i) Classify metamorphic rocks based on texture.

(2 marks)

(ii) Define a metamorphic aureole.

(2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** Based on texture, metamorphic rocks are classified into two groups:

1. **Foliated** rocks, in which the minerals are arranged in parallel layers or bands (e.g. slate, schist, gneiss).
2. **Non-foliated** rocks, in which the crystals are interlocking with no parallel arrangement (e.g. marble, quartzite).

**(ii)** A **metamorphic aureole** is the zone of contact-metamorphosed rock that surrounds an igneous intrusion (such as a batholith or a dyke); the heat of the magma has baked and recrystallised the country rock, and the degree of change decreases away from the intrusion.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) (i) Describe a limestone based on the minerals present and texture.

Minerals present: ........ (1 mark)

Texture: ........ (1 mark)

(ii) State ONE use of limestone.

(2 marks)

(iii) Describe a mudstone.

Mineralogy ........

Texture ........

(2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** **Minerals present:** mainly **calcite** ($\mathrm{CaCO_3}$), with a little dolomite or quartz.

**Texture:** fine to medium grained, crystalline (non-clastic) or made of shell fragments (bioclastic); fossils are often visible.

**(ii)** One use (any one): raw material for **cement** manufacture; building stone; making lime for agriculture; crushed stone (aggregate).

**(iii)** **Mineralogy:** mainly **clay minerals** (e.g. kaolinite, illite) with some very fine quartz.

**Texture:** very fine grained (the grains are too small to be seen with the naked eye), smooth, and breaking into blocks or lumps (not splitting into thin sheets as shale does).
